text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The National Convention Executive Council (NCEC), an opposition-backed alliance, and 22 religious leaders give President Daniel arap Moi two days from Tuesday to agree to seven resolutions.
- President Moi urges Kenyans not to panic over the suspension of aid to Kenya by the International Monetary Fund.
- The Law Society of Kenya calls on Kenyans to reject the Constitution of Kenya Review Commission Bill published by the attorney-general that seeks to overhaul the constitution.
- Opposition party FORD-Kenya asks the NCEC to call off the national strike for Friday.
- Kenyan Sally Barsosio wins the women's 10,000 metres gold medal at the World Athletics Championships in Athens.
- A Nairobi court is told a Nairobi magistrate solicited one million shillings from the proprietors of a hospital.
- Kenya's national trade union body, the Central Organisation of Trade Unions, warns Kenyan workers from joining Friday's strike.
- President Moi calls for proper management of the country's resources for sustainable economic development.
- The crisis facing the air transport industry worsens as a go-slow by air-traffic controllers entered into its fourth day. ($1=64.25 Kenyan Shillings)
